newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones aims corporate news at PCs via Web.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones aims corporate news at PCs via Web.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co Inc said Thursday it would offer its DowVision corporate desktop news delivery service via the Internet beginning in January.

Dow Jones' Business Information Services unit said its DowVision service would offer a package of news from Dow sources, including the Wall Street Journal, plus front-page headlines from other top U.S. papers and the Financial Times.

Dow Jones officials said the company planned to market its World Wide Web-enabled product to corporate users at prices starting at $100 a month per subscriber for groups as small as 15 users, with lower prices for larger numbers of subscribers.
DowVision is a four-year-old product with more than 100,000 subscribers, according to Dorthea Coccoli Palsho, president of Dow Jones' Buinesss Information unit.
The product is targeted at corporate readers, including executives, sales agents and public relations representatives, the company official said.

The DowVision product competes with news delivery systems from WavePhore Inc, which have added Web access to their existing delivery systems, and an emerging class of Web-centered delivery systems from companies such as Pointcast Inc.
DowVision's move on to the Internet follows the launch of the Wall Street Journal Interactive edition earlier this year.
